headline: Genomic surveillance resolves resistance and lineage in clinical bacterial pathogens
label: Bacterial Pathogen Genomic Evolution
summary: Sequencing workflows for resistance detection and strain typing are being benchmarked against reference pipelines across major bacterial pathogens.
synthesis: Recent items converge on comparative genomics of clinical bacterial pathogens, with resistance determinants and lineage structure as the recurring analytic focus. Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii studies link resistance and virulence features to respiratory versus bloodstream infection and to lineage-associated mobilization of carbapenemase determinants. Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates from disseminated, urogenital, and rectal infections differ in iron-acquisition and type IV secretion genes. Methodological work addresses the surveillance layer: nanopore verification for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, concordance of targeted sequencing with whole-genome sequencing for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, plasmid reconstruction from short-read assemblies, and reproducible WDL workflows for Candida typing. The newer element is validation of accessible sequencing and analysis tools against established reference approaches, applied to clinical isolate collections and open portals such as TBpop.
